THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)

The captioned appeal is by the Insurance company questioning the quantum as well as liability passed by the NC:
2024:KHC-K:9610 Tribunal in MVC.No.1405/2022 on the ground that there is breach of policy condition.

2. The facts leading to the case are as under:
One Abdul Majeed who is the father of claimants died in a road traffic accident dated 08.09.2020.
Claimants contended that deceased was aged about 50 years and was doing mason work and was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Hence, filed a claim petition.
The Manager Cholamandalam vs Wajeed And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34735865/

entities.text: Manager Cholamandalam vs Wajeed And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 3. Though Insurance company strongly disputed its liability on the ground that driver of the offending vehicle did not possess driving licence.

Tribunal however by holding that Insurance company is liable to indemnify owner of the offending vehicle proceeded to award Rs.5,50,000/-
under the head 'loss of dependency'.

In all, Tribunal awarded Rs.6,60,000/-.
4.
This appeal is primarily on two counts.

Firstly, counsel appearing for the Insurance company contends that liability of Insurance company stands absolved in the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9610 light of there being a fundamental breach of policy condition.

The second limb of argument advanced by the counsel is in fact that claimants admittedly being major sons, no compensation could have been awarded under the head 'loss of dependency'.
5.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the claimants would however, counter the contention on liability by placing reliance on the Full Bench judgment rendered in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Yallavva1.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Yallavva1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
While countering second objection raised by the Insurance company that major sons are not entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency', he would place reliance on the judgment relied in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Birender & Others2.
6.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Birender & Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance company and learned counsel appearing for the claimants.
Perused the records.

The issue as to whether the primary liability of Insurance company in satisfying the award is taken away only on the ground that there is breach in policy condition is given a quietus by the Full Bench of this Court in the judgment rendered in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Yallavva.

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Yallavva
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, this Court is of the view that in the light of the law laid down by the Full Bench,
the appellant/Insurance company dehors violation of policy condition is primarily liable to satisfy the award and then recover from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, on liability, the appellant/Insurance company is liable to succeed to that limited extent.

8. Now coming to quantum, this Court is of the view that the appellant/Insurance company's contention that both children being major are not entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' is also dealt with by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birender & Others.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birender & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The available records clearly indicate that the claimants in this case do not belong to an affluent background.
The first claimant, as per the evidence, was working as a laborer at the time of the accident, while the second claimant was pursuing his studies.
The deceased, who was the primary earning member of the family, was engaged in the occupation of a mason, contributing significantly to the household's financial stability.
These facts highlight the economic vulnerability of the claimants.
Notably, both children, though major at the time of the accident, were aged approximately 30 and 25 years respectively.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the landmark case of The Manager Cholamandalam vs Wajeed And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34735865/
3

entities.text: Manager Cholamandalam vs Wajeed And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birender & Others, has categorically held that the right of major children to seek compensation under the head of 'loss of dependency' is not negated solely due to their age or earning status.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birender & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The judgment emphasizes that even if major sons are earning,
they are entitled to claim such compensation, taking into account their relationship with NC:
2024:KHC-K:9610 the deceased and their dependency on the deceased's financial contributions.

10. In the light of the principles established by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforementioned case, it is evident that the economic status and circumstances of the claimants play a crucial role in determining their entitlement to compensation.

Considering the facts of the present case, it is apparent that the claimants, who come from a financially modest background, cannot be disqualified from claiming compensation merely because they are major.
Section 166(1)(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act does not impose such a restriction.
The economic dependency of the claimants on the deceased, particularly given their limited means and vulnerable position, warrants recognition.
Accordingly, this Court holds that both claimants are entitled to compensation under the head of 'loss of dependency,' notwithstanding their status as major children.
The economic reality and the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9610 dependency relationship between the deceased and the claimants are pivotal in arriving at this conclusion.

11. In the light of principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court is of the view that claimants are infact entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'.
12.
Be that as it may.
The accident is of the year 2020.
The compensation awarded under the head 'loss of dependency' is fair and just and may not warrant interference at the hands of this Court.
